prompts: Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: English Study Buddy Lesson 2.4 learning illustration. Create a polished landscape educational infographic titled "From evidence to understanding". Warm white background, navy text, muted teal and restrained amber, clear adult-learning editorial style, spacious layout, big readable English typography. Main flow: "Evidence" (source and analysis notebook icon) → "Interpretation" (thoughtful analyst icon) → "Audience" (technical colleague and decision-maker illustrations) → "Action" (a proposed decision with a question, not a completed check). Under Evidence: "Source • method • limits". Under Interpretation: "What does it mean?". Under Audience: "Adapt detail, keep the facts". Under Action: "Recommendation + uncertainty". Lower strip titled "Choose language that matches the work" with four short cards: "Present — general facts", "Past — completed work", "Future — planned work", "Conditional — hypothetical outcomes". Footer: "Clear language. Traceable claims. Honest limits." Depict conceptual documents without numerical charts, fake results, logos, screenshots, or completed student work. Use only specified short English labels, avoid decorative microtext.

Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: English Study Buddy Task 2.4 team workflow learning illustration. Create a polished landscape infographic titled "Task 2.4 — Team roles and handoffs". Warm white background, navy text, muted teal and restrained amber, spacious professional adult-learning style and readable English labels. Four connected cards, left to right: "Anna + Chris" / "Dataset shortlist" with two thoughtful colleague silhouettes and dataset cards; "Ben" / "EDA evidence" with analyst and a magnifier over a blank grid; "Anna + Chris" / "Comprehensive report" with a document, split sublabels "Anna: structure" and "Chris: visuals"; "Team leader" / "Stakeholder speech" with a speaker addressing a small audience. Arrows signify evidence handoffs, with an unobtrusive return feedback arrow. Bottom two panels: "Speech manuscript" / "At least two pages" / "Approximately 800–1000 words"; and "Choose your route" / "Hypothetical leader, real group, or solo Anna / Ben / Chris". Footer: "Plans are not completed findings. Keep sources and limitations visible." Do not imply learner must perform all roles or that real collaboration occurred. No numerical data, fake outcomes, checkmarks marking completed work, software screenshots, brand logos or extra text.
